articles.title: White-Hot Glass
articles.summary: Black body with flowing molten silver-gold folds and heavy sparkle, like glowing liquid metal. Reads as black obsidian with large glowing gold-copper patches; the fine ripples blur into a warm metallic gold with a pinkish glow against the black.
articles.what: White-hot glass flowing in blinding silver-fire folds over a black obsidian body. FRACTURED FORGE. Up close: Two zones: a big patch of tightly wound topographic ripple lines in copper-gold with pale cream and pink contour edges, like oil-slick or wood burl, and a black zone with faint dark-grey ripples of the same shape. The edge between them is a soft smoky boundary. From a distance: Reads as black obsidian with large glowing gold-copper patches; the fine ripples blur into a warm metallic gold with a pinkish glow against the black. Measured spec (average): metal 143, roughness 58, coat 96. Shine: gloss. Metal: medium. It brings its own colours.
when: Best on: hood, body, hero panel.
Fits: show car, gt / sports car, stock car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "White-Hot Glass" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood and roof: big patches need large flat panels
Side panels: the black-to-gold boundary reads as a graphic edge
White numbers read on the black zone; gold or pale numbers vanish on the bright ripples, so use a solid plate.
Fine scratches or grain on the black zone: adds a second texture
Pairs well with: chrome, red, white, gold.
pitfalls: Not flames: no tongues or licks, only ripple contours
Not silver-white: the bright zone is copper-gold with pink, not silver
Avoid: big dark areas in the sim, numbers over the sparkle.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 143 (strong pearl or anodized metal), roughness 58 (high gloss), clearcoat 96 (satin or weak clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and roughness and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: big dark areas in the sim, numbers over the sparkle.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: fine scratches or grain on the black zone: adds a second texture; wide stripes: cut across the two zones cleanly
Patterns to avoid: other contour, swirl or flame patterns: they fight the ripples
Spec overlays that work: gloss clearcoat on numbers: contrast against the glassy ground; none on body: spec is already varied
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.
